subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Dan Cong: Phoenix Oolongs
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Dan Cong: Phoenix Oolongs.

hook.text: Phoenix Mountain in Guangdong, China, grows oolongs that naturally mimic the aroma of orchid, honey, and fruit.

buildup.text: Dan Cong means 'single bush.' Each tree produces tea with a distinct aroma—no two trees taste the same.

discovery.text: Some trees are centuries old. The oldest Dan Cong trees produce tiny amounts that sell for extraordinary prices.

twist.text: These teas mimic flavors like grapefruit, ginger flower, and almond—without any added ingredients.

climax.text: Dan Cong production is risky. One mistake in charcoal roasting can ruin a batch worth thousands of dollars.

punchline.text: One bush, one aroma, unrepeatable. Nature's originals.

quiz.question: What does 'Dan Cong' mean?
options: Single bush—each tree has its own unique character
